J U D G M E N T :

This petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation of .50,00,000/- for the death of Bhargav T.V. S/o T.B.Venkataramireddy @ T.B.Venkatarama Reddy in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners is that on 02-08- 2024 at about 7:40 a.m., the deceased, Bhargav T.V.
was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No. KA- 07-S-2262 near Katevaripalli Cross, Addagal,
Srinivasapura Taluk, Kolar District.
At that time, the driver of a KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-07-F-1456 (herein referred to as the offending bus) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to severe impact of the accident, Bhargav sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Immediately after the accident, the dead body was shifted to Govt. hospital, Gownapalli, where post- mortem examination was conducted, and thereafter the dead body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed the last rites and obsequies ceremonies.
3.
The petitioners submit that, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents, petitioner No.3 is the grand mother and petitioner No.4 is the brother of the deceased.

The deceased was aged about 18 years,
hale and healthy and was a college student cum part time worker at Sree Venkateshwara Motor Waring shop at Chintamani, earning a sum of Rs.20,000 per month.

The petitioners were financially and emotionally dependents on the deceased, and due to his untimely death, they have suffered severe mental shock, agony, loss of love and affection, and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.

The petitioners further state that, they incurred an expenditure of about Rs.1,00,000/-
towards transportation of the dead body, funeral, and obsequies ceremonies.
It is the specific contention of the petitioners that, the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent being owner cum and insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
5. The Respondent in the written statement has denied the negligence of its driver.
It is contended that, the offending bus was proceeding near Katevaripalli Cross in a slow and cautious manner by observing all traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, the rider of the motorcycle was allegedly Venkatarami Reddy Allias T.B. ... vs K.S.R.T.C on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92832928/

On noticing the same, the driver of the bus is stated to have immediately taken the bus towards the extreme left side of the road and brought it to a halt in order to avoid the accident.

However, despite taking such precautionary measures, the deceased, due to over-speeding and loss of control over the motorcycle, dashed against the front right corner of the KSRTC bus, which resulted in the accident and the unfortunate death of the deceased.
The respondent has therefore contended that, the alleged accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself and not on account of any fault on the part of the bus driver.

6. Further, the respondent has also denied the age, occupation, and income of the deceased as stated in the petition and and has further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive,
exorbitant, and without any basis.
Hence, on these grounds, the respondent has prayed for dismissal of the claim petition against it with costs.

2. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what amount ?
3. What order or award ?

9.

At that time, the driver of the offending bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased.
Due to severe impact of the accident, Bhargav sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
12. Petitioner No.1, being the father of the deceased, was examined as PW.1.

He filed his affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief under Order XVIII Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
reiterating the averments made in the claim petition.

In support of his case, he relied upon the police documents marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P8, namely FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, vehicle seizure mahazar, inquest report, post-mortem report and charge sheet.

13. On the other hand, the respondent has contended that, the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the deceased himself, who allegedly rode the motorcycle at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, without wearing a helmet, and was unable to negotiate the curve.
It is further contended that, the deceased crossed the midline and came to the extreme right side of the road.
According to the respondent, upon noticing the same, the driver of the bus took the vehicle to the extreme left side and brought it to a halt in order to avoid the accident.

However, despite such precautionary measures, the deceased allegedly lost control due to over-speeding and dashed against the front right corner of the KSRTC bus, resulting in the accident and his death.
14. In order to substantiate the said contention, the driver of the KSRTC bus was examined as RW-1.
He reiterated the defence taken in the written statement in his chief affidavit.
15. During the course of cross-examination of PW- 1, several suggestions were made to the effect that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased.
PW-1 denied the same and asserted that, the accident occurred due to high speed and negligent driving of the bus driver.
He admitted that, his son sustained head injuries and succumbed to the same but denied the suggestion to the effect that the deceased was not wearing a helmet and that he was riding at high speed.
He further denied that, his son had come completely to the right side of the road and that he himself collided with the bus.
He also denied the suggestion that the deceased was not having driving experience and that he was a minor at the time of the accident.
He further denied the allegation that the police, in collusion with the petitioners, had falsely filed the charge sheet against the bus driver.
16. The respondent has produced three documents, namely photographs of the bus, a complaint allegedly lodged before the Superintendent of Police, Kolar, and the postal receipt.
On perusal of the photographs, it is evident that, the front right portion of the bus was damaged.
However, the bus was found stationed on its proper side of the road.
17. It is pertinent to note that, though the accident occurred on 2.08.2024, the complaint to the Superintendent of Police was lodged only on 08.02.2024.
No satisfactory explanation has been offered by the respondent for the delay in lodging the said complaint.
Further, if really the accident had occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, the respondent could have examined independent witnesses or any passengers in the bus to substantiate the defence.
No such independent evidence has been placed on record.

sentences.text: On careful perusal of the entire material available on record, it is seen that after due investigation, the jurisdictional police have filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending bus.
The respondent has not produced any cogent material to disprove the police records or to probabilize their defence.
Nothing substantial has been elicited in the cross-examination of PW-1 to discredit his testimony.
19. It is well-settled that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation, and strict proof of negligence as required in criminal trials is not necessary in claim proceedings.
The standard of proof is one of preponderance of probabilities.
The filing of the charge sheet against the driver of the offending bus prima facie establishes negligence on his part.

20. From the oral and documentary evidence placed on record, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending KSRTC bus.
Accordingly, it is held that the driver of the offending bus was negligent in causing the accident, and due to the said accident, Bhargav died as a result of the injuries sustained.
Hence, this Issue is answered in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.2:- Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents, Petitioner No.3 is the grand mother and petitioner No.4 is the brother of deceased.
In order to substantiate their relationship, PW-1 has produced the inquest report, Aadhaar cards of the deceased and Petitioners, they are marked at Ex.P.9 to 13.
The recital of the said record shows that deceased Bhargav was the son of Petitioner No.1 and 2 and brother of the petitioner No.4.

Petitioners have stated that, the deceased was hale and healthy, was a college student cum part time worker at Sree Venkateshwara Motor Waring shop at Chintamani, earning a sum of Rs.20,000 per month.
The petitioners, being financially and emotionally dependents on him, have suffered immense mental shock, agony, loss of love and affection, and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.

22. On perusal of records, it is found that Petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased at Ex.P.9, which shows the date of birth as 18-06- 2006 and as such, age of the deceased is considered as 18 years at the time of accident and appropriate multiplier applicable is 18.
23.
It is stated that the deceased was hale and healthy, he was a college student cum part time working at Sree Venkateshwara Motor Waring shop at Chintamani, earning a sum of Rs.20,000 per month.
The petitioners, being financially and emotionally dependent on him, have suffered immense mental shock, agony, loss of love and affection, and loss of the sole breadwinner of the family.
To substantiate the income and avocation of the deceased, the Petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of proof of income, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Since the accident has been occurred in the year 2024, notional income Rs.16,500/- per month is taken for the assessment of compensation.
24. As the deceased was aged about 18 years, future prospects of 40% is to be added on the income of the deceased as per Pranay Sethi case.
Then, the income would be .23,100/-.
Since, deceased was bachelor, 50% of his income shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
